name: Battlezone Regulator/Audio II PCB
drawing: DP-156 sheet 1 Side A, Regulator/Audio II PCB Schematic 035435-02 Rev B
coverage: Read in full from sheet 1 Side A. No board map is published for this one: it is a discrete board that does not use the A-R grid, and its designators are Q1, Q2, Q3, Q5, Q7, Q8, Q9 -- 'Q' is a valid grid row letter, so feeding these to build_board.py would place transistors as if they were grid ICs.

Q1.note: voltage regulator, 8-pin can; the reference for the whole +5V logic supply

Q3.note: current source power transistor; this is the one that gets hot

Q5.note: first audio amplifier, gain of ten, into J8 speaker output

Q7.note: second, independent audio amplifier, same circuit and gain

CR5-CR8.note: bridge off the 36VAC input, giving the unregulated +/-22VDC

R8.note: the +5V adjustment, with R7 (7.5k) and R6 (2.9k) around it

rails.in: 36VAC on J9 pins 4 and 5; +10.3VDC unregulated on J6 pins 3, 5 and 6
rails.out: +5V REG and +5V RTN on J7; +12VDC, +22VDC, -22VDC, -5VDC and GND on J10; speaker pairs on J8

notes: This is a third Battlezone board, separate again from the game PCB (035742) and the Auxiliary PCB (035678-01). It does two unrelated jobs: it regulates the +5V logic supply for the game PCB, and it amplifies the audio coming back from the Auxiliary PCB.

The regulator senses remotely. +SENSE and -SENSE are high-impedance inputs taken directly from the +5V and ground inputs at the game PCB, so what is regulated is the voltage at the game PCB, not at the regulator -- that is what cancels the IR drop along the harness. It also means a bad harness or dirty edge connector shows up as the regulator's own output climbing while the game PCB still reads 5V.
Two independent TDA2002AV amplifiers, Q5 and Q7, each with a gain of ten and its own speaker pair on J8. One dead channel is one amplifier, not the sound generation on the Auxiliary PCB.
The +22V that the Auxiliary PCB's audio output stage runs on comes from here, off the 36VAC bridge -- unregulated.

R8: Connect a voltmeter between the +5V and GND test points of the game PCB.
Adjust R8 on the Regulator/Audio PCB for +5 VDC on the voltmeter.
Connect a voltmeter between +5V REG and GND on the Regulator/Audio PCB. It must not read more than +5.5 VDC. If it does, clean the edge connectors on both the game PCB and the Regulator/Audio PCB.

If cleaning does not close the gap, measure GND to GND between the two boards, then +5 REG to +5V between them. That shows which harness wire or connector is dropping the voltage; troubleshoot that one.
